statement: On exercise of a nonstatutory (nonqualified) stock option that did not have a readily determinable fair market value at grant, the service provider includes as ordinary compensation income the fair market value of the stock received (less any restriction other than one that never lapses) minus the sum of the amount paid for the stock and any amount paid for the option; for employees that income is wages subject to employment taxes and income tax withholding.
caveat: Options with a readily determinable FMV at grant, substantially nonvested stock received on exercise (where § 83 timing and an 83(b) election apply), and transfer-restriction facts change the timing and amount. Educational statement of the Publication 525 rule — not advice on any actual exercise.
